summary: Timor-Leste's Migration Service says travellers of all nationalities, except those subject to separate visa waiver arrangements, may apply for and, if they satisfy the criteria, obtain a tourist visa on arrival, valid for 30 days' stay and extendable once for the same period; the fee is US$30, paid in US$ cash. It says the visa can be obtained at all official border posts, air, land or sea, that are open to foreign nationals and have a Migration Service presence. Schengen Area citizens travel visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period (citizens of the United Kingdom and Ireland are not included), and citizens of Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand are visa exempt for stays of up to 30 days for tourism purposes.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says the visa costs 30 US dollars, payable only in cash. The Migration Service says EFTPOS and credit card facilities are not available and ATMs and currency exchange may not be, so have the correct amount in US$ cash when you arrive.

For the overland crossing from Indonesia at Atambua-Batugade, the UK Foreign Office says you can purchase a visa on entry, and the Migration Service says the tourist visa can be obtained at land border posts that are open to foreign nationals and have a Migration Service presence. Australia's travel advice says that if you enter by land from West Timor (Indonesia), you'll need to get a visa before arrival.

The UK Foreign Office says roads are generally in poor condition, that main routes are often single-track mountain roads which can deteriorate quickly and become impassable, particularly during the rainy season, and that outside Dili you should travel in convoy whenever possible. It says that if you hire a car it's likely you'll have to hire a driver as well.

The UK Foreign Office lists health risks in Timor-Leste including rabies (Oecusse exclave, Bobonaro and Covalima municipalities, and possibly elsewhere), chikungunya, dengue, gastroenteritis, typhoid, hepatitis and tuberculosis. It says medical services are limited, particularly outside Dili, and that in a medical emergency it's likely you'll need to be evacuated to Australia or Singapore.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Timor-Leste?
faq.answer: Timor-Leste's Migration Service says travellers of all nationalities, except those subject to separate visa waiver arrangements, may apply for and, if they satisfy the criteria, obtain a tourist visa on arrival, valid for 30 days' stay; the fee is US$30. Foreigners who have previously been refused entry, removed or excluded, or who have outstanding fines, must obtain the visa before seeking entry. Schengen Area citizens travel visa-free for 90 days in any 180-day period (citizens of the United Kingdom and Ireland are not included), and citizens of Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand are visa exempt for stays of up to 30 days for tourism purposes.

faq.question: What do I need for the visa on arrival?
faq.answer: The Migration Service says that where the visa is applied for on arrival you must present an acceptable travel document valid for at least 6 months at the date of entry and a completed arrival declaration and, if requested, evidence of sufficient funds, of accommodation arrangements, and of departure arrangements such as an onward transportation ticket or booking. The fee is US$30, paid in US$ cash.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Timor-Leste?
faq.answer: The Migration Service says that in normal circumstances the tourist visa may be extended once only, for a further stay period of 30 days. The fee is US$40, you apply in person at the Migration Service Headquarters in Dili, and processing takes up to 15 days. The UK Foreign Office says to apply, if possible, at least 15 days before the tourist visa's expiry date.

faq.question: What currency does Timor-Leste use?
faq.answer: The US dollar, according to the Government of Canada, which also says the economy is primarily cash based, that many places will not accept bills issued prior to 2007, and that credit cards are not widely accepted. The UK Foreign Office says notes printed before 2009 are usually rejected but can be changed at the Central Bank in Dili.

faq.question: Can I cross overland from Indonesia to Timor-Leste?
faq.answer: The Migration Service says the tourist visa can be obtained on arrival at all official border posts, air, land or sea, that are open to foreign nationals and have a Migration Service presence, and the UK Foreign Office says that if you enter through Indonesia at the Atambua-Batugade border crossing you can purchase a visa on entry.
